title: Variational Bayesian Flow Network for Graph Generation
claim: A structured, leakage-free precision construction feeds a coupled Bayesian update solved as one linear system, replacing factorized updates.
layout: 2 stacked panels, left-to-right flow, math in boxes, heatmap matrices
description: Two stacked panels with a left-to-right flow. Panel (a) starts with a small graph G=(X,A) showing true edges (solid) and virtual edges (dashed). Arrows lead to a dependency-graph box that links node indices X to edge indices A with dotted lines. Next is a green-shaded Laplacian matrix, element-wise masked by a diagonal matrix M. The flow then splits into two red-shaded heatmaps, the prior precision and the observation precision. Each heatmap has a 'Regularized + εI' box. Panel (b) has a green sender/receiver distribution box with Gaussian formulas. A red-outlined Joint Bayesian Update box holds the precision equations. From there, arrows run to an SPD linear system icon and an iterative solver chip icon. The next stages are a blue posterior belief parameter box and a core network prediction box. A feedback arrow carries the consistency loss back to the sender/receiver box. The eye goes first to the colored matrices and the central red box.
caption: Illustration of VBFN framework. (a): From $G=(X, A)$, construct a no-leakage dependency graph $\mathcal{H}$, assign edge weights $\{w_{uv}\}$, and form the masked weighted Laplacian $\bm{\mathcal{L}}$. Then instantiate $\bm\Omega_{\mathrm{prior}}$ and obtain $\bm\Omega_{\mathrm{obs}}$. (b): With fixed message precision $\bm\Omega_{\mathrm{obs}}$, sender–receiver message–matching defines the training loss, while inference uses a coupled Bayesian update solved by iterative solvers.
abstract: Graph generation aims to sample discrete node and edge attributes while satisfying coupled structural constraints. Diffusion models for graphs often adopt largely factorized forward-noising, and many flow-matching methods start from factorized reference noise and coordinate-wise interpolation, so node-edge coupling is not encoded by the generative geometry and must be recovered implicitly by the core network, which can be brittle after discrete decoding. Bayesian Flow Networks (BFNs) evolve distribution parameters and naturally support discrete generation. But classical BFNs typically rely on factorized beliefs and independent channels, which limit geometric evidence fusion. We propose Variational Bayesian Flow Network (VBFN), which performs a variational lifting to a tractable joint Gaussian variational belief family governed by structured precisions. Each Bayesian update reduces to solving a symmetric positive definite linear system, enabling coupled node and edge updates within a single fusion step. We construct sample-agnostic sparse precisions from a representation-induced dependency graph, thereby avoiding label leakage while enforcing node-edge consistency. On synthetic and molecular graph datasets, VBFN improves fidelity and diversity, and surpasses baseline methods. The reproducible code is available at https://github.com/Cello2195/VBFN.
